levie.en:
Sorry to anyone who thought AI would mean we’d work less (at least for now). AI makes it easy to explore more than you did before, and so you start doing far more as a result.

I regularly have seemingly small things that end up quickly consuming 3 hours because the agent made it easy to get started, but you still have to do the rest of the work to complete the project.

This is work that I wouldn’t previously have handed out to anyone else, it’s just stuff that never got done because it took too long to do fully manually. And, counterintuitively, for some of these tasks as AI gets good enough at doing them, it even becomes economically worth it to hire someone to do it on an ongoing basis with agents. But until you could try doing them at a low cost you would never have tried.

This is why AI won’t automatically reduce work in the way we imagine because work isn’t static. Most companies have far more they can do than they have today, it was just hard to get started on it all because of the natural constraints of time and labor availability.
levie.zh:
对于那些认为人工智能意味着我们会减少工作量的人（至少目前如此），我深表歉意。人工智能让你比以前更容易探索更多内容，因此你开始做更多的事情。

我经常会遇到看似很小的事情，但最终很快就消耗了 3 个小时，因为代理让上手变得很容易，但你仍然需要完成其余的工作才能完成项目。

这是我以前不会交给其他任何人的工作，它只是从未完成的事情，因为完全手动完成需要很长时间。而且，与直觉相反的是，对于其中一些任务，随着人工智能足够擅长完成这些任务，雇佣某人与代理一起持续完成这些任务在经济上甚至变得值得。但除非你能尝试以低成本做到这一点，否则你永远不会尝试。

这就是为什么人工智能不会像我们想象的那样自动减少工作，因为工作不是静态的。大多数公司可以做的事情比今天多得多，但由于时间和劳动力可用性的自然限制，很难开始做这一切。

adityaag.en:
How does one make sense of SF?

We are living through the craziest computing revolution of the last 2 decades....and 95% of the value being created is within a 4-mile radius in SF (h/t @eladgil )

It's just hard to understand....why is the concentration so high?

What is it about this place? There are good reasons that people will offer...good universities, great companies, talent networks, venture capital yada yada yada

But all of that is hard to emotionally understand.

I tend to try to answer these questions through my own lived experience.

Two things happened this week that brought it home for me.

On Wed evening, two GOATS of the design world (@soleio  and @rsms ) did a design talk at SPC.

I saw some other GOATS at the talk (@aaron_ , @benbarry )

And you realize that these GOATS are just so curious about the world. They just want to build and learn. And give back. And with an air of humility and passion. It's so so cool and inspiring.

And then this week we had someone release a mind-bendingly amazing demo of every pixel being generated.



People were blown away but @eddiejiao_obj  and @zan2434  had been jamming creatively for a bunch of time @southpkcommons . 

And in that entire time, they were surrounded by a culture and environment and ecosystem that says "that is crazy but my god, if it works, then what could happen"

There is wonder, amazement and curiosity.

And passion.

I wish this city were cleaner and better governed (but Dan Lurie is crushing).

We are so lucky to be surrounded by weirdos who love to build.

This is why we are who we are.
adityaag.zh:
如何理解 SF？

我们正在经历过去 20 年里最疯狂的计算革命......所创造的价值的 95% 都在 SF 4 英里半径内 (h/t @eladgil )

真是难以理解……为什么浓度这么高？

这个地方到底是怎么回事？人们有充分的理由提供...好的大学、伟大的公司、人才网络、风险投资 yada yada yada

但所有这些在情感上都很难理解。

我倾向于尝试通过自己的生活经历来回答这些问题。

这周发生的两件事让我想起了这一点。

周三晚上，设计界的两位山羊（@soleio 和 @rsms）在 SPC 上进行了设计演讲。

我在演讲中看到了其他一些山羊（@aaron_，@benbarry）

你会发现这些山羊对这个世界非常好奇。他们只想构建和学习。并回馈。并且带着谦逊和热情的气息。这太酷了，太鼓舞人心了。

然后本周，我们有人发布了一个令人费解的令人惊叹的演示，展示了正在生成的每个像素。



人们被震撼了，但 @eddiejiao_obj 和 @zan2434 已经创造性地即兴创作了一段时间 @southpkcommons 。 

在整个时间里，他们被一种文化、环境和生态系统所包围，这种文化、环境和生态系统说“这很疯狂，但我的上帝，如果它有效，那么会发生什么”

有惊奇、惊奇和好奇。

和激情。

我希望这座城市更清洁、管理得更好（但丹·卢里（Dan Lurie）令人崩溃）。

我们很幸运，周围都是热爱建造的怪人。

这就是我们之所以成为现在这样的原因。
